messages:

Date: 2026-05-17T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Aligning Commit/Best Case/Pipeline — definitions + quick workshop

Hi team,

Finance flagged a few discrepancies during the weekly forecast scrub: deals that are clearly contract-signed are still showing up as "Best Case," and some opportunities with signed LOIs are in "Commit." Before the biweekly close I want us to standardize how we label Commit vs Best Case vs Pipeline so forecasting is consistent across AMs and regions.

Proposed immediate changes (please review):
- Commit: Legal/Contract signature executed OR customer has submitted a PO and finance has acknowledged receipt. No outstanding pricing/terms approvals.
- Best Case: Verbal agreement + clear implementation plan + legal review in progress; no signature or PO yet.
- Pipeline: Early-stage interest, demo completed or scheduled, no execution-level commitment.

Examples to read in the attached playbook. I put together a short deck with decision rules + CRM examples (attachment: 20260520-forecast-playbook-v1.pdf). Also added a one‑pager with quick-call decision trees.

Action items:
- Please review the playbook and add two live examples from your books to the shared Drive link by EOD 5/19.
- Join a 30-minute alignment workshop on 5/20 at 3:00 PM PT — calendar invite attached. If you can’t make it, we’ll record and circulate notes.

Goal: unified definitions live in the CRM and a short training so managers can coach AMs next week.

Thanks,
Rachel

Rachel Kim
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwood.com)

Thanks Rachel — quick clarifying question: if an opportunity has an LOI signed but legal still needs to finalize SOW details (timeline/SLAs) and the customer says they'll sign the final SOW within two weeks, should that be Commit or Best Case under the new language?

On Mon, May 17, 2026 at 9:02 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi team,
> 
> Finance flagged a few discrepancies during the weekly forecast scrub...

My read is LOI + explicit customer intent should be Commit if there is no outstanding price negotiation and there's an explicit mutually agreed start date. If legal work is purely editorial (timelines, contact names) and there is an executed LOI, we typically treat as Commit. But let's iron out the boundary in the workshop — I can pull two current LOI deals to walk through.

– Rishi

Adding a concrete example from my book: DEAL-4971 (AcmeCorp).
- Current state: Legal has signed the commercial terms, customer sent scanned signature but procurement says PO will arrive in 10 business days. HubSpot notes: "Signed agreement received (scanned), PO pending." Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/DEAL-4971

My suggestion: If the commercial agreement is signed by both parties (even if the PO is pending), we should consider this Commit; otherwise teams are under-crediting ARR in weekly forecasts. If Finance needs the PO for revenue recognition we should have a separate flag in CRM rather than moving it out of Commit.

Happy to walk through in the workshop and present this case.
